DFG 2D-2 benchmark (Um=1.5 -> Ubar=1.0, Re=100): unsteady vortex shedding, run to fixed endTime=5s (residualControl never triggers by design -- flow doesn't reach a steady state). wall_time_s is the final ExecutionTime logged at t=5s (16-way parallel); max_courant is the true peak grepped across the full run. Stats from plot_results.py (see that script for the window rationale): Cd/Cl extrema use the saturated tail t>=4.0s (amplitude was still slowly growing from rest before that -- checked by eye and confirmed via per-cycle Cl max: 0.826, 0.891, 0.911, 0.945, 0.954, 0.953, nearly flat only by the last 1-2 cycles); Strouhal number uses the wider t>=3.0s window since shedding frequency is unaffected by the amplitude growth, giving more zero-crossings to average over. Results (t>=4.0s): Cd mean=3.2022, range=[3.1711,3.2337]; Cl range=[-1.0014,0.9675] (max|Cl|=1.0014). Strouhal (t>=3.0s, 5 periods): T=0.3325s -> St=D/(Ubar*T)=0.3007. Matches published DFG 2D-2 reference ranges closely (St~0.300, c_D,mean~3.2, c_L,max~1.0). delta_p corrected 2026-09-14 to follow the actual DFG benchmark definition -- NOT a plain time-average/range over the saturated window (that gave a misleadingly narrow-looking 2.453 mean/[2.4115,2.4946] range from mixing values across the oscillation). Benchmark defines delta_p = p(front)-p(rear) evaluated at t0+T/2, where t0 is a time at which Cl attains a local maximum. Found each Cl local max at t0>=4.0s (parabolic-vertex refinement for sub-sample accuracy: t0=4.3154s, 4.6480s, 4.9809s), evaluated at t0+T/2 using T=0.3325s from the Strouhal calc above (interpolated into the pressure-probe series; the third t0's half-period point falls past t=5s so only 2 of the 3 peaks contribute): delta_p samples [2.468752, 2.469314] -> mean 2.469033 (tight agreement, spread <0.001). delta_p from probes at (0.15,0.2)/(0.25,0.2), rho=1 (kinematic pressure); no established reference value tracked here (2D-2 benchmark literature this project consulted emphasizes St/Cd/Cl over delta_p) -- recorded for completeness/future comparison only. DFG 2D-3 benchmark: same case/mesh as 2D-2, but inlet ramped by an extra sin(pi*t/8) time factor from rest (0/U's codedFixedValue), controlDict endTime changed 5->8s, otherwise unchanged (Um=1.5, nu=1e-3). Not periodic like 2D-2 -- one ramp-up/ramp-down transient over the full 8s window. wall_time_s is the final ExecutionTime logged at t=8s (16-way parallel); max_courant is the true peak grepped across the full run. lift_coefficient_Cl/drag_coefficient_Cd columns here are the run's maxima (the standard DFG 2D-3 reported quantities), not a saturated-window mean like 2D-2: Cd max=2.9632 at t=3.92s, Cl max=0.4803 at t=5.72s (from postProcessing/forceCoeffsDict/0/forceCoeffs.dat, full time series -- required foamPostProcess -func forceCoeffsDict -parallel run directly against the processorN/ decomposed data rather than reconstructing every one of the 402 written time steps first, since foamRun.fish only reconstructs -latestTime by default). Matches published DFG 2D-3 reference values closely (ref. c_D,max~2.9483, c_L,max~0.4651 -- within ~0.5% and ~3% respectively). delta_p is the other standard DFG 2D-3 reported quantity: pressure difference (front-rear stagnation probes, same (0.15,0.2)/(0.25,0.2) locations as 2D-1/2D-2) evaluated at the LAST time step t=8s specifically (not a saturated-window/half-period calc like 2D-2, since this case isn't periodic) -- by t=8s the sin(pi*t/8) forcing has returned to 0 and the flow is decaying back toward rest, so delta_p(t=8) checks how close the solution gets back to equilibrium. delta_p=-0.131359 (p_front=-0.962977, p_rear=-0.831618).
